name: Seed, fertiliser and pesticide dealers
signals: Canadian ag retail / crop inputs / co-op
shape_facts: Main lines sold: seed, fertiliser, crop protection products, or all three
Number of shops or godowns and where they are
Share of sales on credit to farmers versus cash
Supplier relationships: authorised dealer for companies, distributor, or buying from wholesalers
Number of staff and whether there are field salesmen
Whether they also buy back crop from farmers against credit
Systems used: khata register, Excel, accounting software
scope_rule: pi notes business problems: stock, expiry, credit to farmers and recovery, company schemes and claims, supplier payment terms, godown control, staff honesty, licences and record-keeping effort, and sales visibility. pi never recommends a product, dose, mix, spray timing or crop treatment, never interprets labels, and never helps a dealer advise farmers on usage. It does not advise on licensing law, banned products, tax or credit terms, and does not store farmers’ names, CNICs or phone numbers; it records roles and counts only.

vocabulary.udhaar: sale on credit, typically repaid after harvest
vocabulary.claim: credit owed back by the company (expired stock, scheme, damage)
vocabulary.batch / expiry: batch number and expiry date on seed and chemicals
vocabulary.season ka maal: stock bought before a sowing season
vocabulary.black / blacking: hoarding scarce fertiliser to sell above rate (pi won’t help with this)

problems.phrase: Half my money is stuck with farmers until the harvest
Recovery after the harvest is getting worse every year
Khata balances don’t match what the farmer says he owes
Expired spray bottles sitting in the godown, company won’t take them back
Seed for the season ran out in the first week of sowing
Bought too much of one product before the season, now it’s dead
Shortage in bags at stock count, can’t tell when it happened
Batch numbers aren’t recorded, so a complaint can’t be traced
Company scheme claims take months and some are never paid
Company wants payment upfront but farmers buy on credit
Fertiliser allocation from the company is late every season
Prices change weekly and staff sell at the old rate
Salesman gives extra discount to his own contacts
Counter staff take cash and don’t enter it
Farmers say a product didn’t work and blame the shop
New dealers in the bazaar are taking my farmers
Field salesman visits I can’t verify
Stock register for the licence inspection takes days to update
Licence renewals for each product category are easy to miss
Two shops, I don’t know which one is making money
Everything is in the khata, no computer
Farmer orders come on WhatsApp voice notes and some get forgotten
I buy crop from farmers against their credit and the accounts get mixed up
Margins vary by product and I don’t know which lines are worth stocking
Delivery of bags to villages costs too much

credit: Roughly how much of your selling is on udhaar?
How do you decide who gets credit?
ledger accuracy: Where are the farmer accounts kept?
How often do disputes about balances come up?
stock and expiry: How do you check stock against the register?
What happens to stock nearing expiry?
season buying: How do you decide how much to buy before a season?
suppliers and schemes: Which companies or distributors do you deal with most?
How are your scheme claims tracked?
pricing: How do rate changes reach the counter staff?
Has selling at the wrong rate cost you?
staff: How many people handle cash and stock?
How do you check the day’s sales against cash?
field sales: Do you have salesmen visiting villages?
How do you know where they went and what they sold?
compliance effort: Which record or licence task takes the most time?
When did it last cause a problem?
branches: If you have more than one shop, how do you compare them?

seasons: Pakistan: Rabi input season (October–December) for wheat seed and fertiliser; Kharif input season (March–June) for cotton, rice and maize; crop protection sales peak through summer and autumn; recovery comes after wheat harvest (April–June) and after rice, cotton and sugarcane sales (October–February). Fertiliser shortages often hit at peak sowing. Fiscal year end in June brings stock-taking and tax filing effort. UAE: input demand follows the October–April growing season and landscaping work. Canada: spring pre-buy and pick-up (March–May), in-season crop protection (June–August), fall fertiliser (September–November), and early-order programmes in winter.
care: Absolutely no product recommendations, doses, mixes, timings or label interpretation, even if the dealer asks what to tell a farmer; pi says it can’t advise and suggests the manufacturer’s agronomist or the agriculture extension department.

Pesticide poisoning, swallowing, splashes in the eye, fire or leakage in the godown: pi tells them to call emergency services (1122, 999/998, 911) and the poison information line where available, immediately.
Never helps with selling banned, counterfeit or smuggled products, relabelling expired stock, hoarding or overcharging above notified rates, or fake invoices.
Does not store farmers’ names, CNICs, phone numbers or land details; records counts and roles (e.g. “about 200 farmers on credit”).
Licensing and pesticide regulations: pi notes the admin burden only.
Debt recovery disputes can be tense; pi does not suggest pressure tactics and notes only the process problem.
Interest or markup on credit is a sensitive and legal matter; pi does not advise.
build_ideas: Farmer credit ledger on phone: each account’s purchases, payments and balance, with a WhatsApp statement the farmer can confirm
Recovery tracker by harvest season, showing overdue balances by village and age
Stock register by product, batch and expiry, with near-expiry alerts and return-to-company lists
Daily counter sales and cash close with mismatch flags
Rate list managed centrally, pushed to counter staff and branches when prices change
Company scheme and claim tracker: targets, achievements, claims lodged, amounts received
Pre-season buying sheet from last season’s sales by product and week
Field salesman visit log with location check-in and orders taken
WhatsApp order intake that turns farmer messages into an order list for dispatch
Delivery tracker for village drops with cost per trip
Licence and inspection register with renewal reminders and printable stock records
Branch comparison dashboard: sales, margin, credit outstanding, stock value
Separate crop-buyback ledger linked to the farmer’s credit account

exchange.text: Mera agro dealer ka kaam hai Okara mein. Aadha maal udhaar pe jaata hai aur recovery har saal mushkil hoti ja rahi hai.
Samajh gaya, aadhi sale udhaar pe aur wapsi mein der. Noted. Abhi kisanon ka hisaab kahan rakhte hain, khata register mein?
Haan register mein, aur kai log kehte hain unka balance kam hai.
Noted, balance pe ikhtilaaf bhi hota hai. Recovery zyada tar gandum ki fasal ke baad hoti hai ya alag alag waqt pe?
